subject: Proposal: threshold carve-in and monthly credit banding for Pulse AI
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@pulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: threshold carve-in and monthly credit banding for Pulse AI

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Following up with a first-pass SLA template that addresses the specific coverage constraints you raised. High level summary of the proposal attached (redwood-sla-draft-pulse-20261101.pdf):

- Standard availability: 99.95% monthly uptime for hosted endpoints.
- Carve-in for regional maintenance windows: scheduled maintenance (up to 6 hours/month per region) excluded from uptime calculation if announced >72 hours in advance.
- Credit bands (monthly):
  • 99.95% and above: no credit
  • 99.50% - 99.95%: 5% monthly service credit
  • 99.00% - 99.50%: 15% monthly service credit
  • Below 99.00%: 30% monthly service credit
- Latency SLO: p95 generation <350ms for <1M tokens/day customers; we propose to tier latency SLOs by committed throughput — we'll include a table in the draft.
- Monitoring & evidence: we will provide daily availability logs, token-level latency breakdown, and raw incident timelines for remediation.

I know Pulse requested 99.99% in principle; given your workload profile and our intended reserve capacity, we think 99.95% + scaled credit bands gives a reasonable tradeoff while keeping price predictable. If you need a higher baseline we can discuss a dedicated-reservation overlay (Dedicated pool + firm SLAs) — that will change pricing.

Next steps I suggest:
- You and Procure review the attached draft and pulse-redlines.docx (if you prefer to redline) — we can iterate tomorrow.
- If we can land on the credit bands, legal will finish the small edits and we can route to DocuSign.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync Monday to finalize language.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
(priyom.das@redwood.com)

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-pulse-20261101.pdf (SLA draft — redlines welcome)

From: Elena Rossi <elena@pulse.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pulse.ai>, SRE Team <sre@pulse.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: threshold carve-in and monthly credit banding for Pulse AI

Priyom —

Thanks for sending this over. A few quick notes from Procurement + SRE after internal review (see attached pulse-redlines-20261101.docx):

- Baseline ask: Pulse prefers 99.99% for production traffic; anything lower requires us to push back to our customers. If 99.99% is not feasible on hosted, we want a clear migration path and pricing for a dedicated reservation with the higher SLA.
- Credit math: Procurement wants credits to accrue in a way that offsets our estimated revenue loss for critical outages (they asked for a larger top-tier credit for <99.00%).
- Maintenance carveouts: SRE is OK with scheduled maintenance carveouts if we have a playbook for pre-warn, failover testing, and a blackout schedule.
- Evidence: we require signed access to incident logs and an agreed format for monthly availability reports.

Attaching our redlines for your legal team. Also copy our SRE lead — they will want to validate the latency p95 numbers once you provide the throughput tiers.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Ops — Pulse AI
(elena@pulse.ai)

Attachment: pulse-redlines-20261101.docx (Pulse AI redlines)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@pulse.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: threshold carve-in and monthly credit banding for Pulse AI

Elena / team —

Appreciate the candid feedback. Pushed a focused counterproposal below that I think narrows the gap and keeps deal economics intact; attaching a simple CSV with the credit math (credit-bands-pulse.csv).

Counter outline:
- Baseline availability: 99.95% for hosted by default.
- Accelerated path to 99.99%: offer an optional Dedicated Commitment (3x reserved nodes) that raises baseline to 99.99% with an associated premium (we'll provide cost delta in the next email).
- Adjusted credits: increase the top-tier payout for <99.00% to 40% monthly credit (per your ask) while capping total credits at 100% of one month's committed spend.
- Scheduled maintenance: keep 72-hour notice but include an operational runbook and an annual blackout calendar; if we miss announced failover drills, Pulse gets an automatic 5% credit for that month.
- Evidence: yes to signed incident log access (read-only export) and a standard JSON availability export that can be consumed by your monitoring.

If that sounds close, Priyom and I can draft clean language and route to legal. Happy to run numbers for the Dedicated option if Pulse wants that path to 99.99%.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
(ben.carter@redwood.com)

Attachment: credit-bands-pulse.csv (credit calculations and cap examples)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@pulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: threshold carve-in and monthly credit banding for Pulse AI

Elena —

Thanks — Ben's counter looks like a pragmatic path. A few concrete edits I'll propose to legal so we can move quickly:

1) SLA paragraph: change "Standard availability" to "Hosted availability baseline: 99.95% per monthly billing period, measured across provisioned endpoints for Pulse AI."

2) Credit band changes: adopt Ben's adjusted top-tier (40%) and the 100% cap on monthly committed spend. We'll include an explicit example for a $100k monthly commit so the math is transparent.

3) Maintenance carve-in: 72-hour notice for scheduled maintenance, scheduled windows not to exceed 6 hours per region per month. If Redwood misses an announced failover drill, automatic 5% credit (not cumulative with other credits for the same event).

4) Latency SLOs: add a new table in the SLA Appendix mapping p95 targets to committed throughput tiers (we'll produce the table, link to draft: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-pulse-sla-draft).

5) Evidence & audits: Redwood will provide daily availability exports and a monthly signed availability statement. For deeper forensic requests (full traces) we'll accept a written request with a mutually agreed scope and timeline.

If Pulse accepts these edits, Ben and I will ask legal to assemble the final language and route for e-signature. Can we target legal-ready language by close of day Tuesday? Also proposing a 30-minute sign-off call Wednesday (11/04) at 10:00 PT — please confirm if that works for your team.

-priyom

Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
(priyom.das@redwood.com)

Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-pulse-sla-draft
Attachment: credit-bands-pulse.csv (updated)

From: Elena Rossi <elena@pulse.ai>

Date: 2026-11-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: threshold carve-in and monthly credit banding for Pulse AI

Priyom / Ben —

This looks good and aligns with what Procurement will accept as long as the Dedicated uplift and the migration timeline are clearly documented. Procurement confirmed the 100% cap is acceptable. SRE will review the latency appendix once you publish the throughput tiers.

Please have legal generate the final SOW/SLA with Ben's adjusted credits and the Dedicated option as an addendum. Procurement will expect a DocuSign packet and a one-week review window once it lands. We confirm the 11/04 10:00 PT sign-off call.

Thanks —
Elena

Elena Rossi
